items.label: f02-narrow-mutation-shape
items.front: What does the repository's narrow-mutation shape look like?
items.back: One prisma.$transaction containing the authorization check, a scoped updateMany predicate with the expected version, changed.count !== 1 as the conflict, and the audit write.

items.label: f04-refuse-not-cascade
items.front: Why does the app refuse to delete a task that has comments instead of cascading?
items.back: It makes destructive consequences visible: comments (and a project's tasks) must be removed explicitly first. Audit metadata is kept, but it is not a full snapshot or restore system.

items.label: f03-index-referencing-side
items.front: Does PostgreSQL index the referencing columns of a foreign key for you?
items.back: No. Deleting a membership makes the RESTRICT check search Task by (assigneeId, organizationId). If removals become bulk, add @@index([organizationId, assigneeId]) and confirm with EXPLAIN.

items.label: f01-selection-not-authorization
items.front: 'Selection is not authorization' in this app means what?
items.back: The x-org-id header only selects an organization; the server verifies the token subject and then reads the OrganizationMember row for that organization, which supplies the current role. No row means 403.

items.prompt: A team ADMIN wants to edit the wording of another member's comment. What does the API allow?

choices.text: The edit, because admins can change any team content
Delete it as moderation, but not edit its words
The edit, but the audit row names the original author
Neither: comments are immutable once posted

choices: The edit, because admins can change any team content
Delete it as moderation, but not edit its words
The edit, but the audit row names the original author
Neither: comments are immutable once posted

items.explanation: Allowing an administrator to rewrite another author's comment would misrepresent who said it; authorship differs from moderation.

items.prompt: A user was removed from Cedar an hour ago but still holds a valid token. Their next Cedar request returns what, and why?

choices.text: 403: the membership row is read per request and is gone
200 until the token expires
200 with read-only access
401, because removal revokes the token

choices: 403: the membership row is read per request and is gone
200 until the token expires
200 with read-only access
401, because removal revokes the token

items.explanation: Role is not a global user property baked into the token; it is read per request for the selected organization.

items.prompt: A valid Maple member requests a Cedar task id under a Maple project path. What do they get?

choices.text: 409, because the version does not match
403, because the task belongs to another organization
200, because task ids are globally unique
404: the query is scoped to the selected organization

choices: 409, because the version does not match
403, because the task belongs to another organization
200, because task ids are globally unique
404: the query is scoped to the selected organization

items.explanation: Membership in Maple passes the tenant middleware, but tenant scoping in every query makes another organization's rows not found.

items.prompt: A Cedar task is assigned to a user who exists only in Maple. What does the API respond?

choices.text: 200: any real user can be assigned
403: only owners can assign outsiders
200, and the user is added to Cedar automatically
400: they have no membership in the task's organization

choices: 200: any real user can be assigned
403: only owners can assign outsiders
200, and the user is added to Cedar automatically
400: they have no membership in the task's organization

items.explanation: A real user is not necessarily a member of the selected team; the API check gives a helpful response and the compound foreign key is the database backstop.

items.prompt: Why does the assignee foreign key reference OrganizationMember(userId, organizationId) instead of just User(id)?

choices.text: A User FK proves existence; the composite FK proves membership in the task's organization
To make assignee lookups faster through the composite index that the foreign key creates automatically
Because User ids are not unique across organizations
Because PostgreSQL cannot reference the User table from Task when both tables live in the same schema

choices: A User FK proves existence; the composite FK proves membership in the task's organization
To make assignee lookups faster through the composite index that the foreign key creates automatically
Because User ids are not unique across organizations
Because PostgreSQL cannot reference the User table from Task when both tables live in the same schema

items.explanation: The referenced pair needs its own unique constraint, which is why OrganizationMember carries @@unique([userId, organizationId]).

items.prompt: A Cedar member sends a valid token with x-org-id: demo_maple, an organization they do not belong to. What happens?

choices.text: 403 after a membership lookup, before any project or task query
404, because the organization id is hidden
401, because the token's subject was issued for Cedar and cannot be used with another organization
200 with an empty project list, because every Maple query is filtered by the caller's own memberships

choices: 403 after a membership lookup, before any project or task query
404, because the organization id is hidden
401, because the token's subject was issued for Cedar and cannot be used with another organization
200 with an empty project list, because every Maple query is filtered by the caller's own memberships

items.explanation: The header selects; the membership row authorizes. The only query touching Maple is findUnique on (userId, organizationId).

items.prompt: A task update sends dueDate '2031-02-29' and an extra organizationId field. What does validation do?

choices.text: Accepts the date and ignores organizationId
Accepts it and moves the task to the given organization
Accepts it and rolls the date to March 1
Rejects it: 2031 is not a leap year so Feb 29 is not a real calendar date, and the strict schema also rejects the unknown organizationId

choices: Accepts the date and ignores organizationId
Accepts it and moves the task to the given organization
Accepts it and rolls the date to March 1
Rejects it: 2031 is not a leap year so Feb 29 is not a real calendar date, and the strict schema also rejects the unknown organizationId

items.explanation: Due dates are real YYYY-MM-DD calendar values validated including leap years; unknown properties are rejected rather than passed through to Prisma.

items.prompt: Two clients submit task edits with version 4. The first succeeds (version 5). What must the second client NOT do after its conflict?

choices.text: Silently replace its expected version with 5 and retry the old content, which would overwrite the accepted edit unseen
Export its pending values with their baseline
Keep its draft, because drafts should be discarded on conflict
Show an error, because conflicts should be invisible to users

choices: Silently replace its expected version with 5 and retry the old content, which would overwrite the accepted edit unseen
Export its pending values with their baseline
Keep its draft, because drafts should be discarded on conflict
Show an error, because conflicts should be invisible to users

items.explanation: The conditional updateMany on version gives one winner; the loser keeps its baseline and draft separately and needs an explicit load-current action.

items.prompt: A comment create commits but the connection breaks before the response. The user clicks submit again. What happens?

choices.text: The disabled button prevents the retry entirely
A duplicate comment is created: the transaction guaranteed the commit, not delivery, and there is no durable idempotency design
The first comment is rolled back because the response failed
The second request is rejected as a duplicate by the transaction

choices: The disabled button prevents the retry entirely
A duplicate comment is created: the transaction guaranteed the commit, not delivery, and there is no durable idempotency design
The first comment is rolled back because the response failed
The second request is rejected as a duplicate by the transaction

items.explanation: A disabled button helps with local double clicks but does not solve an ambiguous network retry; the project documents this limit.

items.prompt: The composite FK uses PostgreSQL's default MATCH SIMPLE. What does that mean for an unassigned task, and what is the trap for future composite references?

choices.text: If any referencing column is null the constraint is not checked, which allows assigneeId null; a null tenant column would also skip the check, so keep it NOT NULL or use MATCH FULL
Null columns always fail the check, so unassigned tasks need a placeholder user
MATCH SIMPLE makes the constraint deferrable until commit
MATCH SIMPLE checks only the first column of the pair

choices: If any referencing column is null the constraint is not checked, which allows assigneeId null; a null tenant column would also skip the check, so keep it NOT NULL or use MATCH FULL
Null columns always fail the check, so unassigned tasks need a placeholder user
MATCH SIMPLE makes the constraint deferrable until commit
MATCH SIMPLE checks only the first column of the pair

items.explanation: It is safe here only because Task.organizationId is NOT NULL.

items.prompt: A user is OWNER of Cedar and a regular MEMBER of Maple. They try to change a Maple project. What happens?

choices.text: 200: OWNER anywhere grants owner rights everywhere
403: their Maple role is MEMBER
200: project changes only need membership
404: Maple projects are invisible to Cedar owners

choices: 200: OWNER anywhere grants owner rights everywhere
403: their Maple role is MEMBER
200: project changes only need membership
404: Maple projects are invisible to Cedar owners

items.explanation: Treating role as a global user property would grant incorrect privileges; requireManager checks the per-organization role.

items.prompt: An authenticated request arrives with no x-org-id header at all. What does attachTenantContext return?

choices.text: 401, because the tenant context is missing
200, using the first organization the user belongs to
403, after looking up the caller's default organization
400, before the membership lookup
